issue.title: CONTRIBUTING.md staging command fails on deleted files
issue.body:
The "Safe staging" section ends with `git add -u -- src/counter.ts src/typescript.svg`. Those two files aren't in the repo anymore, so the command now fails with `fatal: pathspec 'src/counter.ts' did not match any files`.

**Where:** `CONTRIBUTING.md`, around line 59.

**Done when:**
- The broken line is removed (or fixed if you find a reason to keep it)
- Running the whole staging block on a fresh clone gives no errors

**Hint:** use `git log` on those two paths to see when they were removed.

explanation.summary: The Safe staging block in CONTRIBUTING.md includes a command that refers to two files that no longer exist, so the command fails on a fresh clone. The issue asks to remove that broken line or fix it if there is a reason to keep it, and to confirm the whole staging block runs without errors.
explanation.why_it_matters: Contributors following the documented steps can stage their changes without hitting an error. Fixing the instructions also prevents confusion about files that are no longer part of the repository.

files.why: This section contains the staging block, including the command that refers to the deleted paths.

files.quote: Then `git status` and confirm `browser-droid/`, `pkg/`, journals, and demo binaries are **not** listed.
files.why: This is the documented check to perform after running the staging block.

concepts.explanation: Staging marks selected file changes to be included in the next commit.
A pathspec is a file or directory name that Git uses to decide which paths a command should operate on.
